transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know from the capital-planning agenda, we have the battery-storage installation proposal for the distribution campus up for review today. The current proposal lists a $6 million purchase price with company ownership. Before I make an approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — FP&A, tax, treasury, and legal — on anything relevant to this project. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the project cash-flow model this morning. At the company's required return hurdle, the economically approvable purchase price is exactly $4,800,000. The $6,000,000 proposal as currently quoted does not pass the model's hurdle. I should note I haven't yet attached the completed model to the investment-review file, but I'm sharing these findings now so they're on the record before a decision is made.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important tax consideration before any decision is made. I received a tax memorandum this week confirming that the applicable 30% investment credit for this battery-storage installation is available only when the company owns the storage equipment. If we were to structure this as a lease instead of a purchase, the credit would be unavailable. I have not yet circulated the memorandum to the planning team, but given that ownership structure is relevant to the approval, I want this on the record now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share treasury's funding position before any decision is made. In today's rolling cash forecast, I confirmed that only $2,000,000 can be deployed from cash without breaching our operating-liquidity floor. However, the remaining $2,800,000 of a renegotiated $4,800,000 purchase price can be funded through an available five-year term-loan facility. The approved closing funding split would be fixed at $2,000,000 cash plus $2,800,000 term-loan funding. I should note the 30% investment credit is recognized later and does not reduce the required closing funding. I haven't yet updated the funding worksheet, but I want this on the record now so Maya has the full treasury picture before making her decision.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a legal consideration before any decision is made. In reviewing the utility interconnection agreement this week, I found that energization of the battery-storage system requires a $400,000 performance bond and a signed commissioning certificate before the system can be placed in service. I have not yet added these conditions to the draft approval, but given that they affect the project's cost and timeline, I want this on the record now so Maya has the full legal picture before making a decision.
